CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right index finger pain from skiing injury.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
The patient is a 42-year-old female who injured her right index finger while skiing last Saturday. She was skiing double black diamond runs when she lost control and fell, jamming her index finger on an object during the fall. She reports pain severity of 7/10. She has taken ibuprofen which did not provide significant relief. She denies application of ice or splinting. She denies other injuries from the fall.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Chronic constipation.
Appendectomy at age 7.

MEDICATIONS
Miralax.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient skis.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right hand x-ray: Normal alignment with all bones and joints in appropriate positions. No fractures identified.
Right index finger: Pain elicited with palpation, traction, and compression over the distal interphalangeal joint.

RESULTS
Right hand x-ray: Normal. No fractures.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Sprain of the distal interphalangeal joint of the right index finger.
1. Splint applied to right index finger
2. Mobic 15 mg once daily, 14 tablets prescribed
3. Follow-up appointment in 2 weeks to reassess healing
4. Hand therapy may be initiated at follow-up if needed
